notes: AArch64 companion to ci/kernels.lock.json, which keeps the two x86-64 lanes and the 25-suite matrix shape. This file is not consumed by ci/run_vm_tests.py; the portability suite (tests/kernel/test_arch_portability.py) reads its lane selection from MOJOBPF_VNG_RELEASE / MOJOBPF_VNG_ARCH / MOJOBPF_VNG_ROOT.

The runner binary is resolved via PATH at run time; its version and SHA-256 must match this lock, and must equal the ci/kernels.lock.json runner (same vng binary drives both architectures). Absolute install paths are intentionally not pinned.

Kernel images are the Ubuntu mainline builds cached by virtme-ng under ~/.cache/virtme-ng/<release>/arm64/; the .deb file names and hashes below identify the exact artifacts. The downloader also fetches the -64k image+modules variants; the lane boots the plain generic image only (uname proves it). A lane whose cache is absent fails the suite; lanes are never silently skipped.

The guest root is the pinned Ubuntu cloud image below, unpacked once with sudo (vng reuses an existing --root dir; it would otherwise download the same URL itself). The suite stages into the root's world-writable /tmp unprivileged and maps it with an explicit --rwdir guestpath=hostpath pair, because virtme rejects host paths outside a cross root.

Every boot provisions its observer from scratch (guest writes are ephemeral): the suite fixes the guest clock from a staged host epoch (the TCG guest boots thinking it is 1970, which makes apt reject every Release file), then apt-get update plus apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends bpftool over user-mode networking. The observed observer versions below are what the archive served on the recorded runs; the suite echoes the per-run versions and the board records them, so archive drift is visible, never silent.

Raw-syscall C holders are built on the host with the pinned cross compiler (they use symbolic SYS_/__NR_ names, so they resolve per target). The in-guest raw bpf() reader selects its syscall number from the guest machine name (321 on x86-64, 280 on AArch64) and refuses anything else.
Correctness only: nothing in this lane measures performance, and emulation timing is never quoted as a performance result.
